content.title: About
content.content: Canned lasagna with meat is a ready‑to‑eat dish packed in a sealed tin. It contains layers of pasta, tomato sauce, cheese, and ground beef or pork. Designed for quick heating in a microwave or on the stove while preserving flavor and texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lasagna originated in Italy during the Middle Ages, and the canned version appeared in the United States in the early 20th century.
Canning allows the dish to be stored for 2‑3 years without added preservatives.
Grated Parmesan often creates a golden crust when the dish is heated.
Cans are usually made of aluminum with a food‑safe inner coating.
Meat lasagna is one of the most calorie‑dense ready meals, providing about 300‑350 kcal per serving.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Ground meat supplies a complete set of essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Hard cheese adds calcium, important for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Tomatoes – lycopene source
items.content: The tomato sauce provides lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that helps protect cells.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: High carbohydrate and fat content makes the dish a quick source of energy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain a lot of salt, which may be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Calorie rich
items.content: The dish is calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑management diets.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese and other dairy ingredients can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Bisphenol A in packaging
items.content: Some aluminum cans may have trace amounts of BPA; choose products from reputable manufacturers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Open the can, pour the contents into a bowl and heat in the microwave for 3‑4 minutes or on the stove, stirring until evenly hot. For extra flavor, sprinkle additional cheese and bake for 5‑7 minutes until a golden crust forms.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer leftovers to an airtight container and consume within 2‑3 days, storing them in the refrigerator.
